contributions: LC-GRPO: an inference-aligned ODE Euler step followed by a Langevin correction as the RL rollout transition for flow models
Recovery of the required score from the flow velocity, needing no additional score model
A proof that one Langevin correction reduces the Wasserstein error of an imperfect ODE Euler step
A comparison showing the proposed transition can beat Euler-Maruyama discretization at matched randomness
Results on SD3.5-Medium, FLUX.1-Dev and HunyuanVideo across text-to-image and text-to-video
limitations: No quantitative results in the abstract. The theoretical guarantees hold 'under suitable conditions' and at a matched randomness level, neither specified here. Evaluation is on image and video generation only; nothing is reported for language models or reasoning. Reward optimization in this setting is measured against learned reward models, whose gaming is a known failure mode not addressed.
method: Each rollout transition first takes an inference-aligned ODE Euler step, then applies a stochastic Langevin correction targeting the marginal at the resulting timestep. The score needed for the correction is recovered directly from the flow velocity, so no separate score model is required, and the resulting transition stays an isotropic Gaussian with a tractable likelihood usable for policy optimization. The paper proves that under suitable conditions one Langevin correction step reduces the Wasserstein error of an imperfect ODE Euler step, and that at a matched randomness level the proposed transition can be more accurate than standard Euler-Maruyama discretization of the reverse SDE.
one_liner: A GRPO variant for flow-based generative models that replaces SDE training rollouts with an ODE step plus a Langevin correction, aligning training samples with the deterministic sampler used at test time.
problem: Flow-based generative models are sampled by solving a deterministic ODE, while online RL needs stochastic rollouts to explore. Existing flow GRPO methods swap the ODE for an SDE during training. The two share marginals in continuous time but their finite-step discretizations differ substantially, and SDE rollouts blur as exploration noise rises, so the samples optimized are not the samples the test-time sampler produces.

relevance.reasoning-training: Off-target for reasoning: the models are image and video generators and no language or reasoning benchmark appears. It matched this topic on the token GRPO alone. The one idea worth carrying over is the framing — that RL exploration noise injected during training changes the distribution the policy is optimized on relative to the deterministic decoder used at test time. Language RLVR has the same structure, since rollouts are sampled at temperature and evaluation is often greedy, and the archive holds no paper that measures that gap directly.

results: On SD3.5-Medium, FLUX.1-Dev and HunyuanVideo, LC-GRPO consistently improves reward optimization on text-to-image and text-to-video tasks, preserves generation quality, and narrows the gap between stochastic training rollouts and deterministic test-time ODE inference. No numbers are given in the abstract.
